schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE SPENDING (
    USER_ID INT,
    SPEND_DATE DATE,
    PLATFORM ENUM('DESKTOP', 'MOBILE'),
    AMOUNT INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (USER_ID, SPEND_DATE, PLATFORM),
    CHECK (AMOUNT > 0),
    CHECK (PLATFORM IN ('DESKTOP', 'MOBILE'))
);
q1: SELECT P.SPEND_DATE,P.PLATFORM,IFNULL(SUM(AMOUNT), 0) TOTAL_AMOUNT,COUNT(USER_ID) TOTAL_USERS FROM (SELECT DISTINCT(SPEND_DATE), 'DESKTOP' PLATFORM FROM SPENDING UNION SELECT DISTINCT(SPEND_DATE), 'MOBILE' PLATFORM FROM SPENDING UNION SELECT DISTINCT(SPEND_DATE), 'BOTH' PLATFORM FROM SPENDING) P LEFT JOIN (SELECT SPEND_DATE, USER_ID, IF(MOBILE_AMOUNT > 0, IF(DESKTOP_AMOUNT > 0, 'BOTH', 'MOBILE'), 'DESKTOP') PLATFORM,(MOBILE_AMOUNT + DESKTOP_AMOUNT) AMOUNT FROM (SELECT SPEND_DATE, USER_ID, SUM(CASE PLATFORM WHEN 'MOBILE' THEN AMOUNT ELSE 0 END) MOBILE_AMOUNT, SUM(CASE PLATFORM WHEN 'DESKTOP' THEN AMOUNT ELSE 0 END) DESKTOP_AMOUNT FROM SPENDING GROUP BY SPEND_DATE, USER_ID) O) T ON P.PLATFORM=T.PLATFORM AND P.SPEND_DATE=T.SPEND_DATE GROUP BY SPEND_DATE, PLATFORM
q2: WITH CTE AS (SELECT USER_ID, SPEND_DATE, SUM(CASE WHEN PLATFORM='MOBILE' THEN AMOUNT ELSE 0 END) AS MA, SUM(CASE WHEN PLATFORM='DESKTOP' THEN AMOUNT ELSE 0 END) AS DA FROM SPENDING GROUP BY USER_ID, SPEND_DATE) SELECT SPEND_DATE, 'DESKTOP' AS PLATFORM, SUM(CASE WHEN CTE.DA>0 AND CTE.MA=0 THEN DA ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_AMOUNT, SUM(CASE WHEN CTE.DA>0 AND CTE.MA=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_USERS FROM CTE GROUP BY SPEND_DATE UNION ALL SELECT SPEND_DATE, 'MOBILE' AS PLATFORM, SUM(CASE WHEN CTE.DA=0 AND CTE.MA>0 THEN MA ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_AMOUNT, SUM(CASE WHEN CTE.DA=0 AND CTE.MA>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_USERS FROM CTE GROUP BY SPEND_DATE UNION ALL SELECT SPEND_DATE, 'BOTH' AS PLATFORM, SUM(CASE WHEN CTE.DA>0 AND CTE.MA>0 THEN DA+MA ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_AMOUNT, SUM(CASE WHEN CTE.DA>0 AND CTE.MA>0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS TOTAL_USERS FROM CTE GROUP BY SPEND_DATE

explanation: Both queries aim to aggregate spending data by platform (DESKTOP, MOBILE, BOTH) for each spend date, calculating total amounts and user counts. Q1 uses a left join with platform-specific grouping, while Q2 uses conditional aggregation in CTEs. The logic aligns: users are categorized into platforms based on their spending patterns, and totals are computed consistently across both approaches.
